why: If you only do the things you already know will work, you leave a lot of opportunity on the table. An experiment is not an experiment if you know the outcome. Some of those bets fail. You often learn more from the miss than you would have from a safe success.

Look for whether someone can tell a two-way door from a one-way door. If the decision is reversible, act. More study after you have enough information is waste. If the decision is irreversible, that is when you {lp:dive-deep} and slow down on purpose.

Bias for Action also looks like initiative. It is walking down the hall when yesterday's message got silence. It is picking up the next useful task while you wait. It is booking the meeting, showing up on time, and not expecting someone else to do the work you can do.

It also looks like impatience when a customer is hurting. You join the investigation before anyone proves it is your team's bug. You do the right thing for the customer without waiting for a permission slip. Calculated risk is the point. Motion without a target is not.
calibrationIntro: Score whether someone moves with calculated risk and then course-corrects. Under is paralysis or passivity. Over is steamrolling, no focus, and a pile of unfinished work.

examples.title: Two-way door, then correct
examples.body: A team can A/B a change, ship it to a slice of customers, and roll it back in an afternoon. The leader does not commission a six-week study. They ship the slice, read the result, and either widen it or revert. That is calculated risk. The irreversible launch to every customer is the door you do not kick open.

examples.title: The experiment that taught more than a win
examples.body: A team spends three years on a new front end for a capability they licensed. Nobody uses it. They shut it down. The useful story is not the failure. It is that they were willing to run a real experiment, call the miss, and stop. If you only fund the sure things, you do not invent.

examples.title: Do not wait for the alert
examples.body: Metrics start to look wrong in the afternoon. The person who has been watching them joins the call before the alert fires, and starts the investigation before anyone assigns a team. Bias for Action is that impatience when a customer is about to get hurt, not a personality that cannot sit still in a meeting.

looksLike.individual: An individual with Bias for Action unblocks themselves. They send the note, then they walk over. They keep a next useful task ready for the idle time. They can tell you which recent decision was reversible, what they did with incomplete data, and what they changed when the result came back.
looksLike.manager: A manager with Bias for Action removes the approval theater that turns two-way doors into projects. They expect calculated risk, they do not punish a well-run miss, and they stop the person who is generating motion without finishing. They also know when to force a pause because the door only swings one way.

deepen: Was the last decision you delayed a two-way door, and if so, why did you wait?
What is the smallest reversible step you could take this week with the information you already have?
When a customer was hurting, did you join before the work was assigned to you, or did you wait for proof it was your bug?
Whose input do you actually need before you move, and whose input are you collecting only to avoid being wrong?
What did you finish in the last month, and what did you start and abandon?
How do you tell a calculated risk from doing the work at any cost?
What did the last failed experiment teach you that a safe success would not have?
When yesterday's message got silence, what did you do instead of sending a second one into the same void?
Where are you still studying after you already have enough information to act?

related.note: Dive Deep on one-way doors. Bias for Action on two-way doors. The skill is telling them apart.
Action that does not finish is motion. Results are the point.
Invention requires experiments, and experiments require a willingness to be wrong.
Speed without judgment is thrash. Judgment without speed is a memo.
Stepping up when the work is unowned is Bias for Action with an owner's signature on it.

blog.title: One-Way and Two-Way Doors
blog.note: If you can walk it back, act. If you cannot, that is when you slow down.
